external_entities.name: duty engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who opens the dispatch console in a browser.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network. They open the dispatch console in their browser.
external_entities.notes: The text does not state how an engineer signs in to the console.

external_entities.name: scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work through a SOAP feed.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.notes: The text does not state how the partner identifies the importer.

processes.name: dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript app opened by duty engineers and used to call the dispatch API and receive live job status.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app and our corporate web host serves it.
processes.notes: The text does not state how an engineer signs in to the console. The API's allowed CORS origins and credential policy are not recorded.

processes.name: corporate web host
processes.description: The corporate web host that serves the dispatch console.
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it
processes.notes: The text does not state the host's exposure or security controls.

processes.name: dispatch API
processes.description: The API called by the dispatch console and schedule importer. It runs in the production control plane and can affect live dispatch operations.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
processes.notes: The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

processes.name: schedule importer
processes.description: A scheduled process that pulls the scheduling partner's SOAP feed, parses XML, archives downloaded documents, and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The importer presents an API token issued when it was built; nobody has rotated it since. The text does not state how the importer identifies the scheduling partner.

data_stores.name: dispatch database
data_stores.description: A database holding job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order, without information about the person behind that token.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: Every job order carries the token or session that created it, and nothing about the person behind that token. How the database is protected at rest is not written down anywhere.

data_stores.name: schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder containing each XML document downloaded by the schedule importer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive
data_stores.notes: The text does not state how the archive is protected at rest.

data_stores.name: corporate file store
data_stores.description: The corporate file store on which the schedule archive is located.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a folder on the corporate file store
data_stores.notes: The text does not state the file store's technology, data classification, or protection at rest.

data_flows.name: open console
data_flows.description: A duty engineer opens the dispatch console in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state the authentication mechanism.

data_flows.name: serve app
data_flows.description: The corporate web host serves the dispatch console application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The dispatch console calls the dispatch API cross-origin.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The console and API are served from different origins. The allowed origins and whether credentials are allowed were not recorded.

data_flows.name: live status
data_flows.description: The dispatch console opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and keeps it open for live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: Nobody recorded whether the socket runs over TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, or whether it checks the engineer's session again after it is open.

data_flows.name: read and write data
data_flows.description: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and creating tokens or sessions

data_flows.name: pull work
data_flows.description: The schedule importer pulls the scheduling partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS every hour.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS
data_flows.notes: The text does not state how the partner identifies the importer or how the importer identifies the partner.
data_flows.data_description: tomorrow's planned work in an XML document

data_flows.name: archive document
data_flows.description: The schedule importer writes each downloaded document into the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive
data_flows.data_description: downloaded XML document containing planned work

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: The schedule importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls. It presents an API token.
data_flows.notes: The API token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where duty engineers sit, the schedule importer runs, and the corporate file storage is located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: The same-company, same-staff zone holding the live estate, where an account can move a crew and change the work a depot does that day.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
trust_boundaries.notes: The control plane is not reachable from the internet. A corporate laptop holds none of the control-plane rights.

trust_boundaries.name: scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: The zone controlled by the scheduling partner, which is another company.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database's classification is confidential.
assumptions.basis: The database contains crew mobile numbers, which are personal data, and tokens or sessions associated with job orders.
